cards.alt: Sample multiple choice card: Weight has k = 0.02. How much extra weight is needed to notice a change from a 250 g baseline?

questions.stem: Fechner's law states that sensation grows with the
questions.explanation: Fechner's law is S = k log I. A square or exponent describes Stevens' power law forms, and a reciprocal would decrease sensation as intensity rises.

questions.stem: A person stops noticing a perfume after several minutes. Which process is most directly responsible?
options: Increase in absolute threshold of the cortex
questions.explanation: Constant stimulation reduces olfactory receptor responding, which is adaptation. Lateral inhibition sharpens contrast, and gate control concerns pain.

questions.stem: Finding a red letter among green letters is fast regardless of how many green letters there are. This indicates
options: Parallel processing for a single feature
questions.explanation: A target defined by one feature pops out in parallel, so the time does not scale with the number of distractors. Serial search would slow with more items.

questions.stem: Which fiber type carries slow, dull, burning pain?
questions.explanation: C fibers are unmyelinated and conduct slowly, so they carry dull, burning pain. A-delta fibers are thin and myelinated and carry the fast, sharp component, A-beta fibers carry touch, and motor neurons are efferent.

questions.stem: Reading a smudged letter as an A in CAT but an H in THE is an example of
questions.explanation: Context supplies expectations that resolve the ambiguity. Bottom-up detection would give the same reading in both cases.

demo_cards.back: The minimum stimulus intensity detected 50 percent of the time. Weaker stimuli are subthreshold.

demo_cards.text: Weber's law: {{c1::delta I}} / {{c1::I}} = {{c2::k}}, where k is the {{c2::Weber fraction}}.
demo_cards.extra: A small k means high sensitivity.

demo_cards.stem: Weight has k = 0.02. How much extra weight is needed to notice a change from a 250 g baseline?
demo_cards.why: JND = k x I = 0.02 x 250 = 5 g. A 2 g change is below threshold at this baseline.

demo_cards.statement: A smaller Weber fraction means finer discrimination.
demo_cards.why: A small k means a small proportional change is detectable, so the system is more sensitive.
